body: C-1 (Critical): the initial fix changed the SessionStart hook to bash "$HOME/..." session. That breaks the byte-exact contract documented in .orchestration/tasks/T3-agent-config-herdr-hook.md:33 -- herdr integration install no-ops only on an exact string match, so `make update` would append a duplicate entry every run and the hook would fire twice. Addressed: use bash '{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/...' session, which render_managed_template expands to the same absolute single-quoted string. Verified with chezmoi cat that ~/.claude/settings.json is now byte-identical and no longer appears in chezmoi status.
author: Claude Code

replies.body: Addressed. Manifest now uses bash '{{ .chezmoi.homeDir }}/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh' session, which render_managed_template expands to the byte-identical string herdr writes. Verified: ~/.claude/settings.json dropped out of chezmoi status and check-agent-runtime.py reports runtime=passed. The interim modify_private_settings.json stale-strip was reverted as unnecessary and prone to oscillating against herdr's ensure step.
replies.author: Claude Code

body: M-1 (Medium): the first guard scanned lines for /Users/ only. It missed Linux /home/<user>/ paths (the exact portability case the change targets), false-positived on flow-style projects mappings and trailing comments, and mis-tracked nested projects blocks. Addressed: match /(Users|home)/<name>/, only open the exemption when not already inside one, reset on dedent, and initialise projects_indent to None so there is no conditionally-undefined name. Six tests cover reject-macOS, reject-linux, allow-homeDir, flow-style, subtree-only exemption, and duplicate detection.
author: Claude Code
